title: Lesson Five: The Rich Invent Money
coreMove: Money is invented when financial creativity turns information, timing, courage, and structure into legal value others have not yet recognized.

exampleSpecs.stakes: seeing market value before incumbents agree
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Alexander Graham Bell and Western Union to show undervalued invention without implying every rejected idea is valuable.

exampleSpecs.stakes: turning a listing into a tested offer instead of a fantasy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use real estate, offers, cash flow, and market timing to show practice rather than guaranteed success.

exampleSpecs.stakes: distinguishing created value from fake currency
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use toothpaste tubes and plaster molds to contrast counterfeit money with legal value creation.

exampleSpecs.stakes: using deal structure to control downside
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show how structuring an offer can be smarter than either freezing or gambling.

exampleSpecs.stakes: separating useful rejection from lazy dismissal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Bell's patent and telephone demand to avoid the false lesson that rejection itself proves opportunity.

exampleSpecs.audience: reader with knowledge but limited capital
exampleSpecs.stakes: using structure when savings alone are not enough
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use a non-real-estate cash-flow opportunity to show that knowledge and structure can matter even when capital is limited.
